acceptance.output_evidence: BUILD HALF DONE. All three objects schema-native. Scope_Declaration carries TWO PLANES (WhatPlane predicate-capable / WhoPlane enumeration-with-provenance) per CRO's cert-shaping note 64627, NOT one grammar with a mode flag -- because the S0 measurement shows the two planes FAIL DIFFERENTLY: a predicate over-includes conservatively and readably; an enumeration under-includes SILENTLY via dead members. S6 absence semantics differ per plane and that difference is the reason they are two: WhoPlane.dead_members() returns THREE states (dead found / none dead / None = NOT ASKED), and collapsing 'not asked' into 'none dead' is the error the object exists to prevent. required_authority_class is never numerically compared and no accumulator parameter exists (P4/m5). GATE HALF NOT DONE.

MY OWN DECLARED LIMIT FIRED AND DID NOT PROTECT ME. The first phase-3 run reported 14 dead and was false-positive on two real seats. The module's limits list already said, verbatim, that a principal leaving no trace in the two sources would read DEAD incorrectly. I wrote the caveat and then quoted the number as though the caveat were a control. Only widening the source set fixed it. CTO's framing: declaring a limit documents it, it does not bound it.

commit-gate DOES NOT CHECK FOR NON-ASCII. A non-ASCII character in a print path crashed phase-3 with a charmap error -- CLAUDE.md's own Code Quality rule, which exists precisely because it breaks charmap. py_compile and ruff will not flag a string literal, so the runtime crash was the only detector. Worth knowing if anyone treats the gate as a non-ASCII guard.
